raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

sgl-router renders and tokenizes chats itself for cache-aware routing and `input_ids` forwarding. MiniMax-M3 and M3.1 went through the generic Dynamo Jinja path instead. That path skips SGLang's M3-specific request handling, so these models stayed in the `Guarded` forwarding scope. This PR adds a MiniMax-M3 renderer to `rust/sglang-processor`, following the `processor-model-parity` skill and checked against fixtures, so every text chat forwards `input_ids`.

## Modifications

- `rust/sglang-processor/src/render/models/minimax_m3.rs` (new): picked by the checkpoint's `model_type == "minimax_m3_vl"` (Python's `is_minimax_m3`), with template detection as the fallback for callers without `config.json` (e.g. a `--chat-template` override, sgl-router's tokenizer files). Covers MiniMax-M3 and MiniMax-M3.1-Flash. It mirrors these steps from `serving_chat.py`:
  - `_validate_minimax_m3_request`: checks `thinking.type`, that a `root` message is first and appears at most once, and that tool calls and tool results pair up (ids as a set).
  - `_normalize_minimax_m3_request`: maps `thinking` and effort aliases onto `thinking_mode` / `reasoning_effort`, both before and after `--default-chat-template-kwargs` merge in.
  - `_canonicalize_tool_message_order(sort_text_runs=True)`: sorts tool results into tool-call order, because the template pairs them by position.
  - Tool arguments are parsed strictly. The template prints scalars with `{{ val }}`, so argument floats are printed as Python's `repr` prints them. This also covers integers beyond 64 bits, which orjson reads as floats.
  - Content is handled as the `openai` content format leaves it, with text parts concatenated as the template's `visible_text` does.
- `ChatFormatter::MiniMaxM3` variant wired through `render/mod.rs`, `loader.rs`, `template.rs`.
- `sgl-router/src/tokenizer/chat_formatter.rs`: MiniMax-M3 renders through the processor (`AllText` scope), with a unit test.
- `tests/scripts/generate_parity.py`: the stub server resolves `is_minimax_m3` from `config.json` instead of hard-coding `False`.
- Fixtures `tests/fixtures/parity/minimax-m3.1-flash.json` (rev `262ae683`) and `minimax-m3.json` (rev `d95e30cb`), 215 cases each, generated from the Python serving path.
- Docs: processor README, sgl-router README / REFERENCE (new MiniMax-M3 section).

Left to the engine (`known_gap` in the fixtures): media, floats in tool schemas (Dynamo's `tojson`), `-0` in tool arguments, `tool_reference` parts in tool results or alone in a turn, and a `chat_template` kwarg.

## Host behavior for declined and rejected requests

The renderer distinguishes two failure kinds, matching what Python does on each host:

- **Validation failures are hard errors.** Requests Python's `_validate_minimax_m3_request` / `apply_chat_template` rejects — a bad `thinking.type`, a misplaced or repeated `root` message, unpaired tool calls/results, reserved `chat_template_kwargs` — fail rendering. The engine 400s them, and sglang-server now does the same instead of falling back to the generic Jinja path (which would silently serve a late `root` or an unanswered tool call).
- **Genuinely unsupported requests decline.** Media, `-0` in tool arguments, `tool_reference` parts, floats printed unlike Python, and content-part lists with no text fall back: on sgl-router the chat leaves the `AllText` scope (engine renders), and on sglang-server the request renders through the generic template. These are the `known_gap` cases above, plus the empty-text-parts decline (a parts list joining to `""` is truthy in the template's content check, so Python renders an empty block rather than the default prompt — see the `system_empty_text_part` / `root_empty_text_part` fixture cases).

Not in this PR: porting the `minimax-m3` reasoning and tool parsers to `src/think` / `src/tool_call`. Until they're ported, the router's `lower_chat` returns `Unsupported("reasoning_parser")` and chats keep the engine's OpenAI route. This PR changes rendering only, for routing and `input_ids` forwarding.

## Accuracy Tests

Rendering only; no model forward changes.

- `cargo test -p sglang-processor --test parity` with both checkpoints cached: all 215 cases per fixture match Python on prompt text and token ids (no `token ids not checked` line).
- `cargo test -p sglang-processor --all-features`, clippy `-D warnings` (default and all features), and `cargo check --no-default-features --features render,tokenizer` all pass.
- sgl-router: full `cargo test` passes, and clippy is clean. `chat_render_parity_matrix` runs the existing `minimax-m3.json` router fixture through the new path.
- Not verified against a live M3.1 engine.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Thanks for this. It follows the `processor-model-parity` pattern, and it mirrors `serving_chat.py` rather than any private patch, which is the right reference. I traced `template_args` / `normalize` through both normalization passes (before and after the defaults merge) and the effort and `thinking_mode` results match Python, including when server defaults supply the effort.

Three things I think should be resolved before this lands (inline):

1. **Parity bug:** content parts whose text is empty, in a system or root message, render the template's default prompt (`join_text_parts`).
2. **sglang-server:** a request the M3 renderer declines falls back to the generic template without M3's rules (`template.rs`).
3. **Trigger:** M3 handling is keyed on the template text, but Python keys it on `model_type` (`is_minimax_m3`).

Also: CI hasn't actually run. Every check failed at the label gate because the PR has `documentation` and `rust-processor` but not `run-ci`.

Adding `MiniMaxM3` here means that on sglang-server, a request `render_request` declines goes to `render_chat`'s `NeedsRenderFallback` branch (`rust/sglang-server/src/api_server/http/openai/template.rs`), which calls `render_template`. That generic path has no `_validate_minimax_m3_request`, no `_normalize_minimax_m3_request` and no tool-result reordering.

Concretely:
- `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` plus a tool schema with `"default": 1e-06` (the `tool_float_values` gap) renders the adaptive thinking mode instead of disabled.
- A late `root` message or an unanswered tool call is served instead of rejected with 400 whenever the request also carries `-0` in its arguments or a `tool_reference` part.
- `chat_template_kwargs.chat_template` renders here, but Python rejects it.

The description says these are "left to the engine". That's true for sgl-router, but sglang-server has no engine to fall back to. Options: run `validate` and the normalization in the fallback path for M3, or have M3 declines fail on sglang-server instead of falling back. Either way, could the description say which host behavior is intended?

Python's `is_minimax_m3`, which gates the validation, the normalization and `sort_text_runs`, is `hf_config.model_type == "minimax_m3_vl"` (`serving_chat.py`, in `OpenAIServingChat.__init__`). `template_detection._is_minimax_m3` only picks the parsers. Keying on the template text diverges in two directions:

- A `minimax_m3_vl` checkpoint served with a `--chat-template` that doesn't contain `<mm:think>`: Python still applies the M3 rules, but this PR uses the generic path.
- A fine-tune whose template contains `<mm:think>` but whose `model_type` is different: this PR returns 400 for a late `root` message and injects `thinking_mode`, while Python does neither.

`generate_parity.py` now derives `is_minimax_m3` from `model_type`, so the fixtures can't see this. Could selection key on `model_type`, the way `selection.rs` does for DeepSeek and Kimi? sgl-router's `load_from` already has `config.json` in hand.

Fixed in db0726607a. `join_text_parts` now declines a non-empty parts list whose texts join to "" — as you said, the list is truthy in the template's `{%- if message.content -%}` checks, so Python renders an empty system/root block instead of the default prompt, and flattening to "" would mis-render it. Both fixtures now carry `system_empty_text_part` / `root_empty_text_part` known-gap cases documenting the gap; parity still passes.

Fixed in db0726607a. M3's request-validation failures (bad `thinking.type`, misplaced/repeated `root`, unpaired tool calls/results, reserved `chat_template_kwargs`) are now hard errors rather than declines — Python 400s them on both hosts, and the server has no engine to fall back to, so `render_chat` no longer sends them to the generic template (which would have served a late `root` or an unanswered tool call). Genuine feature gaps (media, `-0`, `tool_reference`, tool-schema floats, empty text parts) still decline to the fallback. Added `minimax_m3_validation_errors_do_not_fall_back` in the server's template tests, and the PR description now states this intended host behavior.

Fixed in db0726607a. M3 handling is now keyed on the checkpoint's `model_type == "minimax_m3_vl"` (Python's `is_minimax_m3`): `ChatFormatter::from_tokenizer_config_with_type` takes the model type, and sgl-router's `ChatFormatter::load_from` passes the one it already reads from `config.json`. Template detection remains only as the fallback for callers without the checkpoint config (a `--chat-template` override, tokenizer files). `loader.rs` has a `minimax_m3_keys_on_model_type` test covering all four combinations.
Renderer looks good, parity passes locally with token ids checked. A few questions inline, mostly about whether some of the router changes in this branch are intended to land here.

#47662 landed on main after your last merge: Python now 400s any reasoning_effort outside low/medium/high/xhigh/max and dropped the none/minimal -> disabled mapping. Is keeping the mapping here intended, or should this follow the new rule and have the fixtures regenerated? effort_none / effort_minimal / kwargs_effort_none currently encode the old behavior.

Is this meant to be part of this PR? It changes breaker policy for every model. The router has no active health prober, so after this a worker that answers 500 to every request (broken mm processor, bad template) is never shed. If it is intended, I'd rather see it in its own PR with that tradeoff spelled out.

inline_comments.body:
Adding `MiniMaxM3` here means that on sglang-server, a request `render_request` declines goes to `render_chat`'s `NeedsRenderFallback` branch (`rust/sglang-server/src/api_server/http/openai/template.rs`), which calls `render_template`. That generic path has no `_validate_minimax_m3_request`, no `_normalize_minimax_m3_request` and no tool-result reordering.

Concretely:
- `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` plus a tool schema with `"default": 1e-06` (the `tool_float_values` gap) renders the adaptive thinking mode instead of disabled.
- A late `root` message or an unanswered tool call is served instead of rejected with 400 whenever the request also carries `-0` in its arguments or a `tool_reference` part.
- `chat_template_kwargs.chat_template` renders here, but Python rejects it.

The description says these are "left to the engine". That's true for sgl-router, but sglang-server has no engine to fall back to. Options: run `validate` and the normalization in the fallback path for M3, or have M3 declines fail on sglang-server instead of falling back. Either way, could the description say which host behavior is intended?

Python's `is_minimax_m3`, which gates the validation, the normalization and `sort_text_runs`, is `hf_config.model_type == "minimax_m3_vl"` (`serving_chat.py`, in `OpenAIServingChat.__init__`). `template_detection._is_minimax_m3` only picks the parsers. Keying on the template text diverges in two directions:

- A `minimax_m3_vl` checkpoint served with a `--chat-template` that doesn't contain `<mm:think>`: Python still applies the M3 rules, but this PR uses the generic path.
- A fine-tune whose template contains `<mm:think>` but whose `model_type` is different: this PR returns 400 for a late `root` message and injects `thinking_mode`, while Python does neither.

`generate_parity.py` now derives `is_minimax_m3` from `model_type`, so the fixtures can't see this. Could selection key on `model_type`, the way `selection.rs` does for DeepSeek and Kimi? sgl-router's `load_from` already has `config.json` in hand.

Fixed in db0726607a. `join_text_parts` now declines a non-empty parts list whose texts join to "" — as you said, the list is truthy in the template's `{%- if message.content -%}` checks, so Python renders an empty system/root block instead of the default prompt, and flattening to "" would mis-render it. Both fixtures now carry `system_empty_text_part` / `root_empty_text_part` known-gap cases documenting the gap; parity still passes.

Fixed in db0726607a. M3's request-validation failures (bad `thinking.type`, misplaced/repeated `root`, unpaired tool calls/results, reserved `chat_template_kwargs`) are now hard errors rather than declines — Python 400s them on both hosts, and the server has no engine to fall back to, so `render_chat` no longer sends them to the generic template (which would have served a late `root` or an unanswered tool call). Genuine feature gaps (media, `-0`, `tool_reference`, tool-schema floats, empty text parts) still decline to the fallback. Added `minimax_m3_validation_errors_do_not_fall_back` in the server's template tests, and the PR description now states this intended host behavior.

Fixed in db0726607a. M3 handling is now keyed on the checkpoint's `model_type == "minimax_m3_vl"` (Python's `is_minimax_m3`): `ChatFormatter::from_tokenizer_config_with_type` takes the model type, and sgl-router's `ChatFormatter::load_from` passes the one it already reads from `config.json`. Template detection remains only as the fallback for callers without the checkpoint config (a `--chat-template` override, tokenizer files). `loader.rs` has a `minimax_m3_keys_on_model_type` test covering all four combinations.

#47662 landed on main after your last merge: Python now 400s any reasoning_effort outside low/medium/high/xhigh/max and dropped the none/minimal -> disabled mapping. Is keeping the mapping here intended, or should this follow the new rule and have the fixtures regenerated? effort_none / effort_minimal / kwargs_effort_none currently encode the old behavior.

Is this meant to be part of this PR? It changes breaker policy for every model. The router has no active health prober, so after this a worker that answers 500 to every request (broken mm processor, bad template) is never shed. If it is intended, I'd rather see it in its own PR with that tradeoff spelled out.

Thanks for this. It follows the `processor-model-parity` pattern, and it mirrors `serving_chat.py` rather than any private patch, which is the right reference. I traced `template_args` / `normalize` through both normalization passes (before and after the defaults merge) and the effort and `thinking_mode` results match Python, including when server defaults supply the effort.

Three things I think should be resolved before this lands (inline):

1. **Parity bug:** content parts whose text is empty, in a system or root message, render the template's default prompt (`join_text_parts`).
2. **sglang-server:** a request the M3 renderer declines falls back to the generic template without M3's rules (`template.rs`).
3. **Trigger:** M3 handling is keyed on the template text, but Python keys it on `model_type` (`is_minimax_m3`).

Also: CI hasn't actually run. Every check failed at the label gate because the PR has `documentation` and `rust-processor` but not `run-ci`.
Renderer looks good, parity passes locally with token ids checked. A few questions inline, mostly about whether some of the router changes in this branch are intended to land here.
